style_when: the article describes one decisive moment or place — a yard at dawn, a control room, a shutdown line, a handover — that a film still could hold
prompt: Split-screen diptych with left-right scenario contrast on a residential driveway. Left half: a wire-free robotic mower sits on sunlit concrete under open sky, a small mast-mounted reference-station antenna beside it casting a long shadow. Right half: the same mower under dense conifer canopy, deep green shadows, no mast visible. 35mm anamorphic wide with dramatic falloff, raking afternoon light from the left, deep pine green, graphite, bone white, concrete and galvanised steel, fine film grain, no people, no text, no logos.
rationale: Cinematic still captures the decisive moment and place of the accuracy failure, while the split-screen diptych renders the two correction scenarios—open sky versus closed canopy—as a single dramatic contrast. The treatment's anamorphic wide framing and atmospheric depth give the residential yard the editorial weight this story needs.
cue: under closed canopy the fix collapses to metres
subject: the unbranded wire-free robotic mower under conifer canopy beside a reference-station mast
core_thesis: A wire-free mower's centimetre accuracy is correction data, not hardware, and under closed canopy the fix collapses to metres unless a reference station with a 135-degree sky cone and power maintains it.
core_conflict: The cloud correction route rated 1–6 cm needs cell coverage, while a reference station rated 1–2 cm needs a mast and open sky; dense tree canopy degrades the fix to metres, making sky view and cell coverage the real constraints.
